In the square-zero case I is a quasi-coherent O_Y-module on the same topological space, so H1 vanishes and A surjects onto B with square-zero kernel. Lifted principal opens are affine inside chosen affine charts, localization gives their rings, and their spectra cover Spec A because the nilpotent quotient preserves primes. For I^m=0, I^(j-1)/I^j is square-zero since 2(j-1)>=j; induction includes m=1 and the empty scheme. No converse defect exists: a closed subscheme of an affine scheme is affine. Item and manifest pre/post hashes agree; only boundary evidence changed. This is audit enrichment, not a mathematical repair. No defect found.

Flatness identifies m-adic graded pieces, fibre injectivity makes f regular by Krull intersection, and the Tor criterion applies because B/fB is finite over B, without demanding B finite over A. For the affine slice, finite-type constructibility and closed z give infinitely many closed image points unless the image is finite. Choosing x distinct from finitely many associated images allows prime avoidance; every cut remains fibre-regular and flat. Pullback is nonempty and proper, so the original affine ideals increase strictly and Noetherianity terminates the construction. A zero fibre is excluded by z in v(Y); an already finite image permits F=X. Pre/post item and manifest hashes agree; the changed boundary evidence is audit enrichment. No defect found.

Finite coefficient contractions of coassociativity give a finite subcomodule containing each v; finite sums give a directed union, including M=0 whose union is {0}. A finite algebra-generating list gives V; coproduct coefficients satisfy the Hopf identities and the antipode matrix inverse, on arbitrary k-algebras. Read three steps, all ten supplier statements and the full global-section equalizer proof. The geometric identity component is clopen in a Noetherian scheme and has a characteristic idempotent. A high p-power descends its finite purely inseparable coefficient extension to k_s; a finite Galois stage fixes the identity component, so linear coefficient independence puts that idempotent over k. Connectedness forces it to be 1. Geometrically reduced groups are smooth by translating a smooth closed point over the algebraic closure, detecting the empty nonsmooth locus, and geometric-regularity descent. Smooth connected then means geometrically integral via disjoint regular components. Nonreduced groups are included only in the connectedness clause. Pre/post item and manifest hashes agree; boundary changes enrich audit evidence. No defect found.

Read all five steps and nine supplier statements; compared full Brion Proposition 2.7.1 proof, https://arxiv.org/html/1509.03059v3#S2.SS7, lines 697–717. Field-flat kernels define a coherent scheme image, and product schematic dominance forces a subgroup. Dense constructible closed-point image contains a dense open on all components; intersecting translates gives all closed points, and constructibility gives topological surjectivity. A trivial scheme kernel makes a monomorphism with reduced singleton geometric fibres; Zariski Main plus closure gives finiteness generically. Source-lifted translations cover the target and give finiteness after algebraic closure; properness of the open source in the finite factor eliminates the boundary and descends finiteness. Finite fibre algebra D tensor D=D has dimension 0 or 1; finite cokernel Nakayama gives the closed immersion. Rational-point kernels alone are not used. Unchanged item/manifest hashes; contract boundary correction is audit enrichment. No defect found.

Read all seven numbered steps and nine supplier statements; checked full Stacks 03BM proof, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03BM, lines 22–41. Groupoid composition conjugates target-evaluation operators on outgoing fibres, so characteristic coefficients are invariants; adjugate telescoping proves Cayley–Hamilton and integrality. The finite-generator Artin–Tate argument makes C finite type. The equivalence-relation monomorphism is essential for the finite closed relation and surjective tensor map. Locally enlarge the residue field by C[T]_(mC[T]); faithful flatness commutes with the equalizer. Semilocal basis selection by CRT and finite avoidance gives t(x_i), and the correctly typed composition tensor relation forces all expansion coefficients into C. Hence A is free and its kernel pair is exactly R after that extension; faithful flatness descends the result. Empty U has empty quotient, while every nonempty rank is positive from identity arrows. Read four steps and seven exact suppliers, including the regular-local normality statement. Checked full Milne AV Theorem 3.2 and Lemma 3.3 proof, printed pp.17–18, https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AV.pdf. Over algebraically closed k, proper target excludes height-one indeterminacy while the group-target divisor lemma forces any nonempty indeterminacy to be divisorial. Therefore none remains. General smooth X may geometrically split; disjoint regular components all meet the faithfully extended schematically dense domain, so their extensions glue. Finite affine chart data spreads to a finite algebraic K/k. Equality of its two pullbacks over possibly nonreduced K tensor K follows by schematic density: injective restriction into k(X) survives tensoring over k. Thus full finite-field descent applies, not merely Galois invariance. Separatedness and reduced dense-domain detection give uniqueness. Pre/post item/manifest hashes agree; changed boundary notes enrich the audit. No defect found.

Read both steps, all twelve suppliers and exact normality/intersection statements. Earlier ample-sheaf and projective-immersion results give a reduced proper projective closure, whose affine normalizations are finite and glue by localization. Over smooth normal G the normalization is the identity, so G is a dense open. The smooth locus of the normal completion contains all height-zero and height-one points over perfect k, leaving codimension at least two. A function there lies in every height-one local ring of every normal affine chart; the S2 intersection lemma extends it globally. Proper integral functions over algebraically closed k are k. No general compactification theorem or projectivity of abelian varieties is used circularly. Pre/post item and manifest hashes agree; boundary notes are audit enrichment. No defect found.

Read six steps, all ten supplier statements and complete Stacks 0BF4, 0BF3 and 0BF2 statements/proofs, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BF4, /tag/0BF3 and /tag/0BF2. The double affine Cech complex computes H1(A×A) as the sum of the two H1(A)'s; axis restrictions are the projections, giving joint injectivity after any residue extension. Triviality of a fibre is equivalent to simultaneous nonzero sections of M and M^-1; finite free nonnegative cohomology complexes make this a closed rank condition. For each square-zero Artinian extension the Cech obstruction is in H1(O) tensor I, vanishes on both axes, and is zero by injectivity. Axis units lift, and normalization at (e,e) makes successive sections unique and compatible. Completion commutes with finite projective terms and kernels, and its faithful flatness transfers a residue-generator lift to the original H0 fibre map. Exact degree-zero base-change then supplies a local section; proper projection removes its zero locus, giving actual open trivializations. Connectedness and pushforward/evaluation glue these to p* N, with N trivial by axis restriction. The cube expression cancels on each identity face up to a one-dimensional scalar line. Arbitrary residue points, imperfect fields, characteristic dividing integers and A=Spec k are included. Item/manifest pre/post agree; corrected boundary notes are audit enrichment. No defect found.

Read both steps and eleven supplier statements, including exact trace nondegeneracy and trace-by-embeddings formulas. Over finite Galois K/k, uniqueness of the largest subgroup makes it semilinearly stable. Trace-dual bases satisfy sum d_i sigma(c_i)=delta_(sigma,1); consequently b=sum d_i sum_sigma sigma(c_i b) expresses every ideal element as a combination of invariant ideal elements. Flat equality glues descended ideals, and group/normality factorization vanishing descends. A nontrivial subgroup over an infinite separable algebraic extension has finitely presented ideal, affine, gluing and group data at a finite separable stage; smoothness descends and connectedness persists into a finite Galois normal closure by geometric connectedness of groups. This contradicts the first case. No assertion is made for inseparable extensions. Item/manifest pre/post agree; boundary changes enrich the audit. No defect found. Perfect k has separable algebraic closure, so the completed separable stability permits reduction to algebraically closed k and properness later descends. A=(Z_red)^0 is smooth connected central; nonproper A would have a positive-dimensional affine subgroup by dichotomy, normal in G by centrality, contradicting pseudo-abelianness. Stable conjugation jets have exact kernel Z, giving a trivial-kernel closed GL immersion of G/Z. Reduced centre components are translates of A, so Z/A is finite, including nilpotents and dimension zero; the exact extension makes G/A affine. A smooth normal almost-complement H has finite kernel into G/A, hence is affine by exact extension. Pseudo-abelianness makes H trivial; A→G is then a faithful flat closed immersion and is an isomorphism. This proves properness without asserting Gamma(G)=k or an affine normal quotient prematurely. The identity centre case and Spec k work. Item/manifest pre/post agree; audit enrichment only. No defect found.
